1.name: Eldritch Invocations
1.notes:
You learn fragments of forbidden lore called Eldritch Invocations.

You gain one invocation of your choice (such as Pact of the Tome) from eldritch_invocation_options.

Prerequisites. Some invocations have prerequisites (such as a minimum Warlock level, a specific pact, or a type of cantrip). You must meet all prerequisites to learn that invocation.

Gaining and Replacing Invocations. As you gain Warlock levels, you learn additional invocations, as shown in the class table. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one invocation you know with a different one for which you qualify. You can’t replace an invocation if it is a prerequisite for another invocation you currently have.

You can’t select the same invocation more than once unless its description explicitly allows it.

1.name: Pact Magic
1.notes:
You form a pact with an otherworldly entity, gaining the ability to cast Warlock spells.

Cantrips. You know two Warlock cantrips of your choice (Eldritch Blast and Prestidigitation are recommended). Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Warlock cantrip. At levels 4 and 10, you learn one additional Warlock cantrip, as shown in the class table.

Spell Slots. The Warlock Features table shows how many Pact Magic spell slots you have and their level. All Pact Magic slots are the same level and never higher than level 5. You regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Warlock spells of level 1+ that you can cast with Pact Magic. To start, choose two level 1 Warlock spells (Charm Person and Hex are recommended). Your number of prepared spells increases as you gain levels, as shown in the class table, and each prepared spell must have a level no higher than your current Pact Magic slot level.
If another Warlock feature gives you spells that are always prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare, but they count as Warlock spells for you.

Changing Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one prepared Warlock spell with another Warlock spell of an eligible level.

Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for Warlock spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Warlock spells.

2.name: Magical Cunning
2.notes:
You can perform a brief esoteric rite for 1 minute. At the end of the rite, you regain expended Pact Magic spell slots up to a number equal to half your maximum Pact Magic slots (round up).
Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

3.name: Subclass Feature
3.notes:
You choose a Warlock subclass and gain its level 3 feature. You gain additional subclass features at higher Warlock levels.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Warlock levels 8, 12, and 16.

6.name: Subclass Feature
6.notes:
You gain a level 6 feature from your Warlock subclass.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
8.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

9.name: Contact Patron
9.notes:
You can now communicate directly with your patron. You always have the Contact Other Plane spell prepared.
With this feature, you can cast Contact Other Plane once without expending a spell slot to contact your patron, and you automatically succeed on the spell’s saving throw.
Once you cast the spell in this way, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

10.name: Subclass Feature
10.notes:
You gain a level 10 feature from your Warlock subclass.

No Subclass Selected
Select a subclass to view its feature(s) here.

11.name: Mystic Arcanum (6th Level)
11.notes:
Your patron grants you a magical secret called an arcanum. You choose one level 6 Warlock spell as your arcanum spell.
You can cast this spell once without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again.
As you gain levels, you gain more arcanum spells (at levels 13, 15, and 17) as shown in the class table. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one arcanum spell you know with a different Warlock spell of the same level.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
12.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

13.name: Mystic Arcanum (7th Level)
13.notes: You gain a level 7 Warlock spell of your choice as an additional arcanum. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot and regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

14.name: Subclass Feature
14.notes:
You gain a level 14 feature from your Warlock subclass.

No Subclass Selected
Select a subclass to view its feature(s) here.

15.name: Mystic Arcanum (8th Level)
15.notes: You gain a level 8 Warlock spell of your choice as an additional arcanum. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot and regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
16.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

17.name: Mystic Arcanum (9th Level)
17.notes: You gain a level 9 Warlock spell of your choice as an additional arcanum. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot and regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

19.name: Epic Boon
19.notes: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

20.name: Eldritch Master
20.notes: Your connection to your patron deepens. When you use Magical Cunning, you regain all of your expended Pact Magic spell slots instead of only half.

1.name: Armor of Shadows
1.notes: You can cast Mage Armor on yourself without expending a spell slot.

1.name: Eldritch Mind
1.notes: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration on a spell.

1.name: Pact of the Blade
1.notes: As a Bonus Action, you conjure or bond with a pact weapon—a Simple or Martial melee weapon of your choice. While bonded, you are proficient with it and can use it as a Spellcasting Focus. When you attack with it, you can use Charisma instead of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls, and you can have it deal Necrotic, Psychic, Radiant, or its normal damage type. The bond ends if you use this feature on another weapon, if the weapon is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more, or if you die. A conjured weapon disappears when the bond ends.

1.name: Pact of the Chain
1.notes: You learn Find Familiar and can cast it as a Magic action without expending a spell slot. When you cast it, you can choose a normal familiar form or a special one: Imp, Pseudodragon, Quasit, Skeleton, Slaad Tadpole, Sphinx of Wonder, Sprite, or Venomous Snake. In addition, when you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack with its Reaction.

1.name: Pact of the Tome
1.notes: At the end of a Short or Long Rest, you conjure a Book of Shadows that only you can use. When it appears, choose three cantrips and two level 1 Ritual spells from any class list that you don’t already have prepared; while you carry the book, you have those spells prepared as Warlock spells. The book can also serve as a Spellcasting Focus. The book disappears if you conjure another with this feature or if you die.

2.name: Agonizing Blast
prerequisites: Known Warlock cantrip that deals damage
2.notes: Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage. You add your Charisma modifier to that spell’s damage rolls. You can select this invocation more than once; each time, it applies to a different eligible cantrip.

2.name: Devil's Sight
2.notes: You can see normally in Dim Light and Darkness—both magical and nonmagical—within 120 feet.

2.name: Eldritch Spear
prerequisites: Known Warlock cantrip that deals damage and has 10+ foot range
2.notes: Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage and has a range of at least 10 feet. When you cast that cantrip, its range increases by a number of feet equal to 30 × your Warlock level. You can select this invocation more than once; each time, it applies to a different eligible cantrip.

2.name: Fiendish Vigor
2.notes: You can cast False Life on yourself without expending a spell slot. When you cast it this way, you don’t roll for the Temporary Hit Points—you automatically gain the maximum value on the die.

2.name: Lessons of the First Ones
2.notes: You gain one Origin feat of your choice. You can take this invocation multiple times, choosing a different Origin feat each time.

2.name: Mask of Many Faces
2.notes: You can cast Disguise Self without expending a spell slot.

2.name: Misty Visions
2.notes: You can cast Silent Image without expending a spell slot.

2.name: Otherworldly Leap
2.notes: You can cast Jump on yourself without expending a spell slot.

2.name: Repelling Blast
prerequisites: Known Warlock cantrip that deals damage via an attack roll
2.notes: Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that requires an attack roll. When you hit a Large or smaller creature with that cantrip, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from you. You can take this invocation more than once; each time, it applies to a different eligible cantrip.

5.name: Ascendant Step
5.notes: You can cast Levitate on yourself without expending a spell slot.

5.name: Eldritch Smite
5.notes: Once per turn when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to deal extra Force damage equal to 1d8 + 1d8 per level of the spell slot. If the target is Huge or smaller, you can also knock it Prone.

5.name: Gaze of Two Minds
5.notes: As a Bonus Action, you touch a willing creature and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn. You can use a Bonus Action on later turns to extend the effect, as long as the creature is on the same plane. While perceiving this way, you gain the creature’s special senses and can cast spells as if you were in your space or the creature’s space, provided you are within 60 feet of each other.

5.name: Gift of the Depths
5.notes: You can breathe underwater and gain a Swim Speed equal to your Speed. In addition, you can cast Water Breathing once without expending a spell slot, regaining the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

5.name: Investment of the Chain Master
5.notes: Your Find Familiar spell summons a familiar empowered by your magic: it gains either a 40-foot Fly Speed or Swim Speed (your choice), can be commanded as a Bonus Action to take the Attack action, can convert its weapon damage to Necrotic or Radiant, uses your spell save DC, and you can give it Resistance to damage it takes by using your Reaction.

5.name: Master of Myriad Forms
5.notes: You can cast Alter Self without expending a spell slot.

5.name: One with Shadows
5.notes: While you are in an area of Dim Light or Darkness, you can cast Invisibility on yourself without expending a spell slot.

5.name: Thirsting Blade
5.notes: You gain the Extra Attack feature for your pact weapon. When you take the Attack action with your pact weapon, you can attack twice instead of once.

7.name: Whispers of the Grave
7.notes: You can cast Speak with Dead without expending a spell slot.

9.name: Gift of the Protectors
9.notes: A special page appears in your Book of Shadows. A creature can spend an action to write its name on it (up to a number of names equal to your Charisma modifier, minimum 1). When a named creature would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, it instead drops to 1 Hit Point, and the page’s magic goes dormant until you finish a Long Rest. As a Magic action, you can erase a name.

9.name: Lifedrinker
9.notes: Once per turn when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage (your choice) and expend one of your Hit Point Dice to regain Hit Points equal to the die roll + your Constitution modifier (minimum 1).

9.name: Visions of Distant Realms
9.notes: You can cast Arcane Eye without expending a spell slot.

12.name: Devouring Blade
12.notes: The Extra Attack granted by your Thirsting Blade invocation now confers two extra attacks instead of one when you take the Attack action with your pact weapon.

15.name: Witch Sight
15.notes: You gain Truesight with a range of 30 feet.
